newsitem.title: BELGIUM: VERMEULEN RAEMDONCK RATES CBR A BUY.
newsitem.headline: VERMEULEN RAEMDONCK RATES CBR A BUY.

text.p: Belgian broker Vermeulen Raemdonck, a unit of BBL, said in a research report on Thursday it had kept its rating of leading cement maker CBR a buy after 1996 results issued late on Wednesday.
The broker said the 1996 earnings per share of 192 francs were above expectations, but that the slight decrease in cash flow raised a question mark.
"We remain however positive on the stock as 1997 should show a further growth in earnings and as the acquisitions in Turkey and China give a real growth profile to the shares," it said.
Group net profit rose 12.1 percent from 1995 to 4.335 billion francs on a turnover up 13.2 percent to 56.352 billion francs. But cash flow fell 1.6 percent.
The company said it would pay a dividend of 95 francs per share, a rise of 9.2 percent from 1995 taking account of the five-for-one share split in May 1996.

The Vermeulen Raemdonck share rating conflicted with that of Generale Bank which said on Thursday it would cut its recommendation on CBR to 'hold' from 'buy' after what it said were disappointing results.
